semantic_evidence.original_quote: Show the PUSCH-related sections and tables (scope for uplink data-channel implementation).
semantic_evidence.finding: The direct objects are sections and their tables. Release-aware sectionId identifies each selected original Section; tableIds identifies the complete directly owned table set for that Section. These two requested roles are required together. Section number/title/level/spec metadata and table captions/content are descriptive provenance, not separate mandatory roles explicitly requested by this navigation question. The grouped answer is an equivalent faithful Section-to-table allocation, including an empty array when the section has no recorded table.
query_clauses: RETURN sec.sectionId AS sectionId, collect(DISTINCT tbl.tableId) AS tableIds

Section_releaseblind_Spec_151_155: rdfs:comment "A 3GPP Technical Specification (TS) or Technical Report (TR). v4.1 (release-aware, hybrid) — a Spec exists in two roles. (1) ABSTRACT HUB: one node per specNumber (IRI tdoc:spec/{specNumber_}, e.g. tdoc:spec/38_211), no tdoc:specRelease; the stable target of release-blind document references — Tdoc/CR MODIFIES & AFFECTS_CORE_SPEC, TRImpact IMPACTS_SPEC/SPEC_IMPACTED_BY (a CR modifies 'the spec', not a single release). (2) RELEASE-KEYED: one node per (specNumber, release) (IRI tdoc:spec/{specNumber_}/{release}, e.g. tdoc:spec/38_211/Rel-15), carries tdoc:specInRelease + tdoc:specRelease + that release's specVersion; the parent of release-specific Sections (BELONGS_TO_SPEC/HAS_SECTION); linked to its hub via tdoc:inReleaseOf. This hybrid preserves release-blind reference edges intact (no re-keying) while giving each release's Sections a release-keyed parent. Pre-v4.0 had a single specNumber node (latest snapshot); v4.0 had only release-keyed nodes (broke hub references) — v4.1 restores the hub additively."@en .

Distinct releases have distinct original Section/Table IDs and remain separate observations. A tableNumber-only array would erase the requested identity and ownership across retained editions; arbitrary caption or row counts are a different unit.
